items.title: Accurate throwing
items.description: Learn to direct a throw by coordinating stance, release, force and follow-through rather than relying on strength alone.
items.oneStarDescription: Land a soft object inside a broad target from a comfortable short distance on 5 of 10 attempts.
items.twoStarDescription: Hit two broad targets at different distances, scoring at least 6 of 10 attempts at each.
items.threeStarDescription: Choose an appropriate throw for two different target locations and complete 8 of 10 attempts within the agreed target zones.

items.title: Active listening
items.description: Understand another person’s point before responding by giving attention, asking clarifying questions and checking your interpretation.
items.oneStarDescription: In a short conversation, let the other person finish and restate their main point in your own words.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask at least two relevant follow-up questions and confirm whether your summary is accurate.
items.threeStarDescription: Summarise the different concerns in a longer conversation and distinguish what was said from your interpretation.

items.title: Add a bill and a tip you chose
items.description: Show this result: add the bill and the tip and read the total.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: add the bill and the tip and read the total.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: add the bill and the tip and read the total.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: add the bill and the tip and read the total.

items.title: Add a finished book to a list
items.description: Show this result: write the title, the author, and the date.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: write the title, the author, and the date.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: write the title, the author, and the date.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: write the title, the author, and the date.

items.title: Add a hanging loop
items.description: Show this result: sew a loop that holds when you hang the object.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: sew a loop that holds when you hang the object.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: sew a loop that holds when you hang the object.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: sew a loop that holds when you hang the object.

items.title: Add a page number
items.description: Add a page number to a short document and show it on two pages.
items.oneStarDescription: Turn on page numbers. A second person can see that this step happened: turn numbering on.
items.twoStarDescription: Show the number on two pages.
items.threeStarDescription: Move the number so it does not cover the text, or say it was already clear.

items.title: Add the map legend's magnetic variation
items.description: After a bearing is set to grid north, rotate the housing by the variation printed in that map's legend.
items.oneStarDescription: Find the magnetic variation note in the legend of the map you are using.
items.twoStarDescription: With the baseplate still, rotate the housing by that amount in the direction the legend states.
items.threeStarDescription: Say you will not turn the housing again while you follow the arrow.

items.title: Add two measurements in the same unit
items.description: Show this result: add them and write the unit.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: add them and write the unit.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: add them and write the unit.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: add them and write the unit.

items.title: Add two numbers on an abacus
items.description: Add two small numbers on an abacus and check the sum in writing.
items.oneStarDescription: Set the first number and say it.
items.twoStarDescription: Add the second number on the abacus.
items.threeStarDescription: Write the sum and compare it with the abacus.

items.title: Address a postcard so the message stays clear
items.description: Write the address on the correct half and leave the message readable.
items.oneStarDescription: Start so someone can see the work: write the address on the correct half and leave the message readable.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: write the address on the correct half and leave the message readable.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave it so another person can check what you did: write the address on the correct half and leave the message readable.

items.title: Address an envelope
items.description: Address an envelope so a postal worker can find the recipient and the return address.
items.oneStarDescription: Write a recipient and an address in the order your postal service shows on its example.
items.twoStarDescription: Add a return address where it will not be confused with the destination.
items.threeStarDescription: Read it as if you did not know the person, and correct one ambiguity.

items.title: Address an envelope you may send
items.description: Show this result: write the address and the return address so both can be read.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: write the address and the return address so both can be read.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: write the address and the return address so both can be read.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: write the address and the return address so both can be read.

items.title: Agree a hand signal
items.description: Agree one hand signal and use it once at a distance where speech is hard.
items.oneStarDescription: Agree what one signal means before you separate.
items.twoStarDescription: Use it once, and have the other person do the agreed response.
items.threeStarDescription: If they do not respond, stop relying on it and use a closer method.

items.title: Agree a photo rule
items.description: Say what may be photographed before people arrive, and where that rule is written.
items.oneStarDescription: Write what is fine to photograph and what is not.
items.twoStarDescription: Place it where people see it as they enter.
items.threeStarDescription: Point to one moment where you followed it or asked.

items.title: Agree a simple exchange
items.description: Agree a small trade or split where both people can point to what they give and get.
items.oneStarDescription: Say what you offer and what you want, and ask the other person to say theirs.
items.twoStarDescription: Change one term, such as time or amount, and restate the whole agreement.
items.threeStarDescription: Write the agreement in two sentences both people accept, including what happens if one person cannot do it.

items.title: Agree a spot for a shared tool
items.description: Agree where a shared tool lives, and put it back once.
items.oneStarDescription: Propose a spot the people who use the tool can reach.
items.twoStarDescription: Agree the spot with at least one other user.
items.threeStarDescription: Use the tool and put it back, or say you left it out and then return it.

items.title: Agree a starting note and hum it
items.description: Show a music-practice result: hum the note someone gives you and stop.
items.oneStarDescription: Arrange yourself so you can hum the note someone gives you and stop.
items.twoStarDescription: Do this once, so another person can hear or see it: hum the note someone gives you and stop.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop when the result is done, without adding a second trick: hum the note someone gives you and stop.

items.title: Agree how you will check in
items.description: Agree with someone when you will contact them and what silence means.
items.oneStarDescription: Propose a time and a channel.
items.twoStarDescription: Agree what you will do if they do not answer.
items.threeStarDescription: Send the check-in at the time, and follow the agreed step if there is no answer.

items.title: Agree where a partner will stop
items.description: Point to the place and see them there before you swim off.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: point to the place and see them there before you swim off.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: point to the place and see them there before you swim off.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the result so another person can check it: point to the place and see them there before you swim off.

items.title: Agree who clears up
items.description: Agree who clears up after a shared task, before the task ends.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask who will clear up before everyone is tired.
items.twoStarDescription: Agree a split or one person, in a sentence.
items.threeStarDescription: Do the part you took, and say if you cannot.

items.title: Air a room and then close the window
items.description: Open a window long enough to change the air and then close it.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up what you need so you can do this: Open a window long enough to change the air and then close it.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete it once so someone else can see the result: air a room and then close the window.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop when the result is done and leave the place usable.

items.title: Align two mirrors to see behind you
items.description: Hold two mirrors so you can see something behind you.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to what one mirror shows.
items.twoStarDescription: Angle the second so you see behind you.
items.threeStarDescription: Name the object behind you that you could not see directly.

items.title: Ambidextrous Skills
items.description:
★ Wrote a sentence with your non-dominant hand.
★★ Wrote a paragraph with your non-dominant hand.
★★★ Wrote different words simultaneously with both hands.

items.title: Annotate a text
items.description: Mark a text with questions and definitions so you can reread only your marks.
items.oneStarDescription: Mark one sentence you do not understand and write the question beside it.
items.twoStarDescription: Look up one hard word and write a short meaning you will understand later.
items.threeStarDescription: Read only your marks and say what the text is about, then check one point against the page.

items.title: Answer as the character
items.description: Answer three questions in a character's voice without adding a new power.
items.oneStarDescription: Write what the character can know.
items.twoStarDescription: Answer three questions inside those limits.
items.threeStarDescription: Refuse one question the character could not answer, and say why.

items.title: Apologize and offer a repair
items.description: Apologize for a specific act and offer a repair the other person can accept or refuse.
items.oneStarDescription: Say what you did, without adding their motive.
items.twoStarDescription: Offer one concrete repair.
items.threeStarDescription: If they refuse or want something else, accept that answer and do not insist.

items.title: Arrange a small display
items.description: Arrange a few objects so a viewer can tell which one is the focus.
items.oneStarDescription: Place one object as the focus and say why the eye should go there.
items.twoStarDescription: Add two other objects that do not steal the focus, and ask a viewer where they looked first.
items.threeStarDescription: Move or remove the object that stole attention, and show the difference.

items.title: Arrange tools in the order you use them
items.description: Lay out the tools for a small task in the order you will pick them up.
items.oneStarDescription: Write the order of tools before you lay them out.
items.twoStarDescription: Place them in that order.
items.threeStarDescription: Do the task and say where the order failed.

items.title: Ask a closed question, then an open one
items.description: Ask one yes-or-no question, then one question that needs a sentence.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask one question that can be answered yes or no.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask one question that needs more than yes or no.
items.threeStarDescription: Write both answers and say which one you will act on.

items.title: Ask a question that gets an answer
items.description: Ask a question that the other person can answer from what they know.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask one question that does not contain two questions, and wait for the answer.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask a follow-up that uses a word the person actually said.
items.threeStarDescription: If the person cannot answer, rewrite the question or stop, and say which you did.

items.title: Ask a question you are willing to stay for
items.description: Show this result: ask one question and stay for the answer.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: ask one question and stay for the answer.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: ask one question and stay for the answer.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: ask one question and stay for the answer.

items.title: Ask a speaker to say it slower
items.description: Show this result: ask once, and stop if they decline.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: ask once, and stop if they decline.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: ask once, and stop if they decline.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: ask once, and stop if they decline.

items.title: Ask before you move their object
items.description: Ask before you move an object that belongs to the person you are helping.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to the object and say what you want to do.
items.twoStarDescription: Wait for a yes, or leave it.
items.threeStarDescription: If you moved it, put it back where they asked.

items.title: Ask before you touch a display
items.description: Ask whether a display may be touched, and keep your hands off until the answer is yes.
items.oneStarDescription: Look for a touch or do-not-touch sign.
items.twoStarDescription: If there is no sign, ask a staff member.
items.threeStarDescription: Touch only after a yes, and describe what you were allowed to touch.

items.title: Ask before you touch a mobility aid
items.description: Show this result: ask, and keep your hands off unless the person says yes.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: ask, and keep your hands off unless the person says yes.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: ask, and keep your hands off unless the person says yes.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: ask, and keep your hands off unless the person says yes.

items.title: Ask for a book that is not on the shelf
items.description: Show this result: ask and write the title.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: ask and write the title.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: ask and write the title.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: ask and write the title.

items.title: Ask for a dissent
items.description: Ask whether anyone sees the decision differently, and record that view.
items.oneStarDescription: After a proposal, ask if anyone disagrees or is unsure.
items.twoStarDescription: Write the dissenting point without arguing it down in the same breath.
items.threeStarDescription: Say whether the decision changed, or that it stood and the dissent remains noted.

items.title: Ask for a name again and use it
items.description: Show this result: ask once more and use the name in the next sentence.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: ask once more and use the name in the next sentence.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: ask once more and use the name in the next sentence.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: ask once more and use the name in the next sentence.

items.title: Ask for a pause
items.description: Ask to pause a conversation and say when you can return.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask for a pause in one sentence.
items.twoStarDescription: Say when you will come back, or that you cannot name a time yet.
items.threeStarDescription: Return at that time, or send an update if you cannot.

items.title: Ask for a story and write it down
items.description: Ask one prepared question about a memory, write the answer, and check it with the teller.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask a question you prepared, and let the person answer.
items.twoStarDescription: Write the answer and mark anything you were unsure you heard.
items.threeStarDescription: Read it back and change what they say is wrong. Do not share it unless they agree.

items.title: Ask for a water refill
items.description: Ask for a refill of a bottle you already have, and stop if the answer is no.
items.oneStarDescription: Show the bottle you want filled.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask once, in a sentence.
items.threeStarDescription: If the answer is no, thank them and stop.

items.title: Ask for directions and repeat them
items.description: Ask for directions and repeat them back so the person can correct you.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask for the way to a specific place, and let the person finish.
items.twoStarDescription: Repeat the steps in order and ask if you have them right.
items.threeStarDescription: Write one landmark they gave you, and what you will do if you do not see it.

items.title: Ask for help specifically
items.description: Ask for a specific kind of help, from a person who can give it, by a time.
items.oneStarDescription: Write what you need, in a form another person could do.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask someone who can actually help, and include a time.
items.threeStarDescription: Record whether they agreed, refused, or offered a smaller help, and thank them.

items.title: Ask for one example
items.description: Show this result: ask for one example and wait.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: ask for one example and wait.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: ask for one example and wait.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: ask for one example and wait.

items.title: Ask if a drink is what they wanted
items.description: Show this result: ask once and change it if they say no.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: ask once and change it if they say no.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: ask once and change it if they say no.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: ask once and change it if they say no.

items.title: Ask someone to name your mark
items.description: Draw a simple mark and write the word another person uses for it.
items.oneStarDescription: Draw a mark with no letters on it.
items.twoStarDescription: Show it and write the word they use.
items.threeStarDescription: Change the mark if their word was not the one you wanted, and test once more.

items.title: Ask the price with a phrase you know
items.description: Show this result: ask and listen for the number.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: ask and listen for the number.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: ask and listen for the number.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: ask and listen for the number.

items.title: Ask what a plaque does not say
items.description: Read a plaque and write one question it does not answer.
items.oneStarDescription: Summarize what it does say in one sentence.
items.twoStarDescription: Write one question a reader still has.
items.threeStarDescription: Say why that question changes how you use the plaque.

items.title: Ask what one word means
items.description: Show a language result: point to the word and ask a person or a dictionary what it means.
items.oneStarDescription: Pick a short text you may use and prepare to point to the word and ask a person or a dictionary what it means.
items.twoStarDescription: Do this once: point to the word and ask a person or a dictionary what it means.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop when you reach a word you will not guess. You did this: point to the word and ask a person or a dictionary what it means.

items.title: Ask what they expect
items.description: Ask what the learner thinks will happen, then show the result.
items.oneStarDescription: Write their expectation before you demonstrate.
items.twoStarDescription: Do the ordinary action and show what happened.
items.threeStarDescription: Ask them what differed from their guess.

items.title: Ask what they want from you
items.description: Ask whether they want a listener, a suggestion, or help, before you offer a fix.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask which of those they want.
items.twoStarDescription: Wait for the answer before you advise.
items.threeStarDescription: Do the job they named, or say you cannot.

items.title: Ask where someone lives and answer for yourself
items.description: Ask a simple where-question and answer it for yourself with a place you can name.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask where the person lives, slowly, in the language you are learning.
items.twoStarDescription: Say where you live, in a short phrase.
items.threeStarDescription: If they do not understand, repeat once more slowly, then stop.

items.title: Ask where the eye went
items.description: Place a title and ask someone where they looked first.
items.oneStarDescription: Put the title at the start of the path you intend.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask one person where they looked first, before you explain.
items.threeStarDescription: If they started elsewhere, move the title and ask again.

items.title: Ask where to put a coat
items.description: Show this result: ask and put the coat where you are shown.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: ask and put the coat where you are shown.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: ask and put the coat where you are shown.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: ask and put the coat where you are shown.

items.title: Ask where to start in a gallery
items.description: Ask a guard or a desk where to start, and follow or adapt their answer.
items.oneStarDescription: Ask where a first-time visitor should start.
items.twoStarDescription: Go to the place they name, or say why you are choosing a different start.
items.threeStarDescription: Thank them and do not keep them from other visitors.

items.title: Ask which side to walk on
items.description: Show this result: ask and walk on the side they choose.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: ask and walk on the side they choose.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: ask and walk on the side they choose.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: ask and walk on the side they choose.

items.title: Assemble and finish scale models
items.description: Assemble and finish a small scale model with attention to fit, alignment, surface preparation and consistent finishing.
items.oneStarDescription: Complete a small kit following its instructions, check alignment and correct visible gaps that affect assembly.
items.twoStarDescription: Prepare the surface as the kit sheet says. Use only a finish that sheet allows in the room you have, and stop if it asks for ventilation or protection you cannot provide. Point to one small area you detailed.
items.threeStarDescription: Complete a more complex model, organise the build sequence, document a challenge and explain how you improved fit or finish.

items.title: Back up and restore personal files
items.description: Make a second copy of personal files and prove you can restore one of them.
items.oneStarDescription: Copy one folder of personal files to a second place and check that the copy opens.
items.twoStarDescription: Delete or rename a practice copy and restore that file from the backup.
items.threeStarDescription: Change one file, make a new copy, and show which version you would use if the working copy were lost.

items.title: Bag a magazine you may store
items.description: Show this result: slide it into a bag without folding a new crease.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: slide it into a bag without folding a new crease.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: slide it into a bag without folding a new crease.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: slide it into a bag without folding a new crease.

items.title: Bag a spare lead by the door
items.description: Show this result: put a spare lead in one place you can find in the dark.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: put a spare lead in one place you can find in the dark.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: put a spare lead in one place you can find in the dark.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: put a spare lead in one place you can find in the dark.

items.title: Balance a book while you kneel and stand
items.description: Show this result: kneel and stand with the book still on your head or in your hands.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: kneel and stand with the book still on your head or in your hands.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: kneel and stand with the book still on your head or in your hands.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: kneel and stand with the book still on your head or in your hands.

items.title: Balance a card on a finger
items.description: Balance a card on one finger long enough to show, then catch it.
items.oneStarDescription: Rest the card and find a still point.
items.twoStarDescription: Hold it still long enough to be seen.
items.threeStarDescription: Catch the card when it tips.

items.title: Balance a fork and explain it
items.description: Balance a fork and spoon or a fork on a glass using a match or a toothpick setup you can explain.
items.oneStarDescription: Put the pieces together.
items.twoStarDescription: Set it on the glass so it stays.
items.threeStarDescription: Point to where the weight sits.

items.title: Balance a hanging mobile
items.description: Hang two objects so a stick hangs level.
items.oneStarDescription: Suspend a stick from one point and see which side drops.
items.twoStarDescription: Move an object or add a small one until the stick hangs level.
items.threeStarDescription: Move one object, show the tilt, and restore the level.

items.title: Balance a spoon on your nose
items.description: Balance a light spoon on your nose for a moment, or say it slid.
items.oneStarDescription: Place the spoon and let go.
items.twoStarDescription: Hold still long enough to be seen.
items.threeStarDescription: Catch it when it slides.

items.title: Balance a stick on a finger
items.description: Balance a light stick upright on one finger for a moment you can show.
items.oneStarDescription: Rest the stick and find where it stays.
items.twoStarDescription: Keep it up long enough for someone to see.
items.threeStarDescription: Take one step and say whether it stayed.

items.title: Balance and weight transfer
items.description: Develop stable posture and controlled weight shifts while standing, stepping and changing direction.
items.oneStarDescription: Hold a comfortable single-leg or split-stance position for 10 seconds on each side, repeating twice beside a stable support.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete five slow weight shifts in different directions, returning to a stable stance after each without grabbing support.
items.threeStarDescription: Perform a short sequence of stepping, pausing and turning in both directions with controlled stops and no loss of balance.

items.title: Balance on one foot while you look up
items.description: Show this result: stand on one foot and look up, then put the foot down when you wobble.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: stand on one foot and look up, then put the foot down when you wobble.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: stand on one foot and look up, then put the foot down when you wobble.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: stand on one foot and look up, then put the foot down when you wobble.

items.title: Balance two weights on a ruler
items.description: Show this result: move one weight until a ruler perched on a fulcrum stays level.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: move one weight until a ruler perched on a fulcrum stays level.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: move one weight until a ruler perched on a fulcrum stays level.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: move one weight until a ruler perched on a fulcrum stays level.

items.title: Ball dribbling and control
items.description: Maintain control of a ball while keeping it moving with repeated hand, foot or implement contacts appropriate to the chosen activity.
items.oneStarDescription: Maintain 10 consecutive controlled contacts with a ball in place or along a short straight path.
items.twoStarDescription: Guide the ball through a line of five wide-spaced markers without losing control more than once.
items.threeStarDescription: Complete a short slalom that includes two deliberate changes of direction and one tempo change while retaining control.

items.title: Ballroom standard dance foundations
items.description: Practise the posture, frame, basic steps and controlled movement used in standard ballroom dance such as waltz or tango.
items.oneStarDescription: Practise a beginner posture/frame and one simple step pattern from a chosen standard dance, solo or with a consenting partner.
items.twoStarDescription: Link two beginner patterns while maintaining a comfortable frame, direction and spacing.
items.threeStarDescription: Perform a short phrase to music with controlled direction changes, timing and awareness of other dancers.

items.title: Barefoot Walker
items.description:
★ Walked 100 steps barefoot on grass.
★★ Walked 5,000 steps barefoot.
★★★ Walked 10,000 steps barefoot.

items.title: Basic baking techniques
items.description: Learn how ingredient handling and mixing methods affect baked results, including kneading dough, rubbing fat into flour, and making batter. This is a technique skill, not a separate skill for every baked dish.
items.oneStarDescription: Measure ingredients and make one simple batter or rubbed-in mixture with the texture described by a trustworthy recipe.
items.twoStarDescription: Make a simple dough and demonstrate controlled kneading until it reaches the recipe’s stated texture, or explain why the chosen mixture should not be kneaded.
items.threeStarDescription: Complete a simple baked item and identify one evidence-based adjustment after evaluating its texture or structure.

items.title: Baste a seam with long stitches
items.description: Baste it so you can pull the thread out later.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: baste it so you can pull the thread out later.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: baste it so you can pull the thread out later.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave or hand on the result so another person can check it: baste it so you can pull the thread out later.

items.title: Baste two layers with stitches you can pull out
items.description: Hold two scraps with long temporary stitches, then take the thread out.
items.oneStarDescription: Pin two scraps and sew a few long stitches that are easy to see.
items.twoStarDescription: Hold the layers and tug once. The stitches should still hold them.
items.threeStarDescription: Draw the thread out and separate the layers.

items.title: Be heard at the back of a room
items.description: Speak so a person at the back can repeat your sentence, without straining.
items.oneStarDescription: Speak one sentence to a person at the back of the room.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask them to repeat it, and try once more if they missed a word.
items.threeStarDescription: If your throat tightens, stop and say you would rest rather than push.

items.title: Bead a repeating pattern
items.description: String a bead pattern of three colors that repeats, and read the pattern back.
items.oneStarDescription: Write the three-color order.
items.twoStarDescription: String at least two repeats.
items.threeStarDescription: Read the colors aloud and stop at a mistake.

items.title: Beatbox a kick and a snare
items.description: Make two different mouth sounds, one for a kick and one for a snare, and alternate them.
items.oneStarDescription: Make one low sound and name it the kick.
items.twoStarDescription: Make a different sound and name it the snare.

items.title: Bind a sketchbook with a band

items.title: Bind a stack with a cover and clips

items.title: Bounce a ball under a leg

items.title: Bounce a table-tennis ball on a bat

items.title: Bounce light with a mirror

items.title: Bow and stop

items.title: Braid a cord

items.title: Observe and identify transport
items.description: Observe aircraft, trains, buses or ships and record useful identification clues, rather than treating every vehicle type as a separate skill.
items.oneStarDescription: Record five transport observations with date, location and at least one visible identification clue for each.
items.twoStarDescription: Correctly identify at least ten observed vehicles using two or more clues where available, and mark uncertain identifications as uncertain.
items.threeStarDescription: Plan a safe and legal observation session, choose a suitable location, organise notes or photographs and produce a concise log that another enthusiast can interpret.

items.title: Observe rocks and geological features
items.description: Practise noticing, describing and comparing rocks and land features during walks, using careful field notes and reliable references rather than relying on appearance alone.
items.oneStarDescription: Record observations for three rocks or exposed geological features, including colour, grain or texture and where the observation was made.
items.twoStarDescription: Use a field guide or trusted reference to propose identifications for five observations and state which clues support each one.
items.threeStarDescription: Complete a short local geology walk log with a simple location map, photographs or sketches, and a clear distinction between observation and interpretation.

items.title: Observe the night sky
items.description: Build a repeatable practice of observing the Moon, stars, planets or major sky events and recording what was visible, when and under what conditions.
items.oneStarDescription: Make three observations on different evenings and record date, time, weather and what you can identify with the unaided eye.
items.twoStarDescription: Use a reliable star chart or astronomy app to identify at least five objects or sky features, checking observations against the reference.
items.threeStarDescription: Plan a short observing session around a target, record conditions and compare observations across at least three dates or sessions.

items.title: Observe wildlife and keep field notes
items.description: Develop a careful field-observation practice by recording visible or audible wildlife clues, using references for identification and respecting the animals and their habitat.
items.oneStarDescription: Make five wildlife observations with date, location, habitat and a description or photograph of the visible or audible clues.
items.twoStarDescription: Use a field guide or trusted identification resource to propose identifications for at least five observations and note confidence or uncertainty.
items.threeStarDescription: Repeat observations at a chosen location on three occasions, use the same recording method and summarise what changed without claiming that the sample represents all wildlife there.

items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: put it in the block or the guard, not loose in a drawer of spoons.

items.title: Store one backup code where you can find it

items.title: Stretch a band and listen
items.description: Stretch a rubber band and say how the sound changed when you plucked it.

items.threeStarDescription: Let it slack again and say whether the first sound returned.

items.title: Striking an object with control
items.description: Practise contacting a moving or stationary object with a hand or appropriate implement and directing its path deliberately.

items.twoStarDescription: Send a slow feed into one of two wide target zones on 6 of 10 attempts.

items.title: String beads and knot a stop
items.description: Show this result: string a short row and knot a stop that keeps the last bead on.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: string a short row and knot a stop that keeps the last bead on.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: string a short row and knot a stop that keeps the last bead on.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: string a short row and knot a stop that keeps the last bead on.

items.title: Strip a bed and pile the linen
items.description: Take the linen off and pile it so the mattress is clear.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up what you need so you can do this: Take the linen off and pile it so the mattress is clear.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete it once so someone else can see the result: strip a bed and pile the linen.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop when the result is done and leave the place usable.

items.title: Strum a rubber-band box
items.description: Stretch bands over a box and play two different notes.
items.oneStarDescription: Put at least two bands on a box.
items.twoStarDescription: Pluck two bands and say which is higher.
items.threeStarDescription: Tighten or shorten one band and say what the note did.

items.title: Summarise a page in two sentences
items.description: Show this result: write two sentences a person could check against the page.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: write two sentences a person could check against the page.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: write two sentences a person could check against the page.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: write two sentences a person could check against the page.

items.title: Summarize a written thread
items.description: Summarize a written thread so a new reader knows the decision and the open question.
items.oneStarDescription: Read the thread and write any decision it contains.
items.twoStarDescription: Write the question that is still open, or say there is none.
items.threeStarDescription: Ask one participant if the summary missed a decision, and fix it if it did.

items.title: Summarize what someone said
items.description: Restate what someone said so they can correct you.
items.oneStarDescription: After someone speaks, say the main point in your own words.
items.twoStarDescription: Ask whether you missed something, and change your summary if they say you did.
items.threeStarDescription: In the summary, separate what they said happened from what they want to happen next.

items.title: Support a climbing plant
items.description: Give a climbing plant a support and tie it so the stem is held, not cut.
items.oneStarDescription: Put a stake or a string in place before the stem bends.
items.twoStarDescription: Tie the stem with a loop that does not pinch, and show a finger of room.
items.threeStarDescription: Look again after the plant has grown and move or loosen a tie that has become tight.

items.title: Swap two events
items.description: Tell two events in the other order and say what the listener now believes.
items.oneStarDescription: Tell two events in the order they happened.
items.twoStarDescription: Tell the same facts in the other order.
items.threeStarDescription: Ask what the listener now thinks caused what, and write their answer.

items.title: Sweep thread snips into a bin
items.description: Sweep them and bin them.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: sweep them and bin them.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: sweep them and bin them.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave or hand on the result so another person can check it: sweep them and bin them.

items.title: Swimmer
items.description:
★ Learned one swimming style.
★★ Learned three different swimming styles.
★★★ Swam a continuous distance of 1km.

items.title: Swimming fundamentals
items.description: Build water confidence, basic floating and propulsion, and the ability to practise a chosen basic stroke in an appropriate swimming environment.
items.oneStarDescription: During a supervised beginner session, practise controlled exhalation, supported floating or body-position exercises chosen by a qualified instructor.
items.twoStarDescription: With instructor approval, travel a short pool distance using a taught basic stroke and return to the wall without panic.
items.threeStarDescription: In a supervised pool, complete a continuous 25-metre swim using a chosen basic stroke, then exit safely using the pool’s normal exit.

items.title: Swing soft poi in one plane
items.description: Swing one soft poi in a flat circle beside your body.
items.oneStarDescription: Keep the circle next to the body, not across the face.
items.twoStarDescription: Change direction and keep the same plane.
items.threeStarDescription: Wrap or catch it against the body without a hit to the head.

items.title: Switch roles in a pair
items.description: Do a task in a pair, then switch who leads and who checks.
items.oneStarDescription: Say who leads and who checks before you start.
items.twoStarDescription: Switch roles for the next part of the task.
items.threeStarDescription: Each person says one thing they noticed in the other role.

items.title: Tailor
items.description:
★ Mended a piece of clothing.
★★ Sewed a simple item from a pattern (e.g., a pillowcase).
★★★ Sewed a complex item of clothing.

items.title: Take a baste out
items.description: Pull the basting thread out and leave the real seam.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: pull the basting thread out and leave the real seam.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: pull the basting thread out and leave the real seam.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave or hand on the result so another person can check it: pull the basting thread out and leave the real seam.

items.title: Take a bin out on the day the card says
items.description: Read the card and take the bin that matches.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: read the card and take the bin that matches.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: read the card and take the bin that matches.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave or hand on the result so another person can check it: read the card and take the bin that matches.

items.title: Take a cue
items.description: Enter or speak when a cue happens, not before.
items.oneStarDescription: Agree the cue, a word or an action, before the run.
items.twoStarDescription: Stay still until the cue, then do the action.
items.threeStarDescription: If you miss it, take the next agreed chance or stop and reset, and say which.

items.title: Take a lead off and hang it
items.description: Show this result: unclip, hang the lead, and watch the animal walk away.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: unclip, hang the lead, and watch the animal walk away.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: unclip, hang the lead, and watch the animal walk away.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: unclip, hang the lead, and watch the animal walk away.

items.title: Take a phone message
items.description: Take a message for someone else with the name, the ask, and the callback.
items.oneStarDescription: Write who called and what they want.
items.twoStarDescription: Read the number or the reply path back to the caller.
items.threeStarDescription: Give the message to the right person and say how urgent the caller said it was.

items.title: Take a photo with a clear subject
items.description: Take a photo in which a viewer can tell what the subject is.
items.oneStarDescription: Take a photo and say what the subject is before you show it.
items.twoStarDescription: Move yourself or the subject so the background does not compete, and show the new frame.
items.threeStarDescription: Name one fault in the first photo, retake it, and show that the fault is smaller.

items.title: Take a soil sample from below the surface
items.description: Take the pinch from about 15 centimetres down, not from the loose surface, then put the hole back.
items.oneStarDescription: Move leaves aside and dig a small hole about a hand's depth.
items.twoStarDescription: Take a small sample from that depth and put it in a clean container.
items.threeStarDescription: Put the soil back and wash your hands.

items.title: Take a soundwalk
items.description: Walk a short way and note the sounds without recording anyone's private talk.
items.oneStarDescription: Walk a short route and write three sounds you heard.
items.twoStarDescription: Say which sound was near, which was far, and which you could not place.
items.threeStarDescription: If you heard a private conversation, do not write the words, and say you left them out.

items.title: Take an offer and add a fact
items.description: In a made-up scene, accept what the other person just said and add one new fact.
items.oneStarDescription: Repeat their fact in your next line without cancelling it.
items.twoStarDescription: Add one new fact that fits, and stop there.
items.threeStarDescription: When they respond, do not drop the fact you added.

items.title: Take back a teaching move
items.description: Make a move, explain it, and put the piece back.
items.oneStarDescription: Start in a way someone can see: make a move, explain it, and put the piece back.
items.twoStarDescription: Complete the result once: make a move, explain it, and put the piece back.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave or hand on the result so another person can check it: make a move, explain it, and put the piece back.

items.title: Take notes for someone you accompany
items.description: Go with someone who asked you to, and write only what they want recorded.
items.oneStarDescription: Before you go, agree what you will write and what you will not.
items.twoStarDescription: Write the points they indicate, in their words as far as you can.
items.threeStarDescription: Give them the notes and delete or leave out anything they say is too private.

items.title: Tap a balloon upward and keep it off the floor
items.description: Show this result: tap a balloon up several times without catching it.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: tap a balloon up several times without catching it.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: tap a balloon up several times without catching it.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: tap a balloon up several times without catching it.

items.title: Tap a brad in scrap and stop if it bends
items.description: Show this result: tap a brad straight and pull it out if it bends.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at what you will change, then start: tap a brad straight and pull it out if it bends.
items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: tap a brad straight and pull it out if it bends.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: tap a brad straight and pull it out if it bends.

items.title: Tap a rhythm and repeat it
items.description: Tap a short rhythm, then repeat it the same way.
items.oneStarDescription: Tap a short pattern and stop.
items.twoStarDescription: Repeat the same pattern once.
items.threeStarDescription: Ask someone to tap it back, and say whether they matched it.

items.title: Tap a word in Morse
items.description: Tap a short word in Morse from a chart you can see, then check it against the chart.
items.oneStarDescription: Choose a word of three or four letters.
items.twoStarDescription: Tap the letters from the chart, with a gap between letters.
items.threeStarDescription: Point back to the chart and correct one mistap, or say it matched.

items.title: Tap two lids
items.description: Tap two lids and say which one rings longer.
items.oneStarDescription: Tap one lid and listen until the sound dies.
items.twoStarDescription: Tap the other lid the same way and say which lasted longer.
items.threeStarDescription: Hold one lid in a different place and say how the sound changed.

items.title: Tape a costume hem
items.description: Tape a temporary hem that holds for a bow and peels off.
items.oneStarDescription: Tape the fold on the inside.
items.twoStarDescription: Bow or walk a few steps.
items.threeStarDescription: Peel the tape and show the cloth.

items.title: Tape a loose music page into the folder
items.description: Show this result: tape the edge so the page turns with the others.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: tape the edge so the page turns with the others.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: tape the edge so the page turns with the others.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: tape the edge so the page turns with the others.

items.title: Tare a scale
items.description: Put a container on a scale, tare it, and weigh one thing inside it.
items.oneStarDescription: Zero the scale with the empty container on it.
items.twoStarDescription: Add one item and read the number.
items.threeStarDescription: Remove the item and say whether the scale returns to zero.

items.title: Taste for salt and stop
items.description: Show this result: taste once and say whether you would add salt, without emptying the salt pot.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: taste once and say whether you would add salt, without emptying the salt pot.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: taste once and say whether you would add salt, without emptying the salt pot.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: taste once and say whether you would add salt, without emptying the salt pot.

items.title: Teach a clap and stop the group
items.description: Teach two people a clap and stop them with a sign you agreed.
items.oneStarDescription: Agree the sign before you start.
items.twoStarDescription: Have them clap the pattern with you.
items.threeStarDescription: Give the sign and see them stop.

items.title: Teach a concept back
items.description: Explain a concept to someone and find the part you cannot yet say.
items.oneStarDescription: Explain one concept without reading, using an example.
items.twoStarDescription: Answer one question, or say you do not know, and mark that spot.
items.threeStarDescription: Check the spot you missed and explain that part again in one clearer sentence.

items.title: Teach a hand position
items.description: Show a hand position for a craft or a piece of music and correct one visible difference.
items.oneStarDescription: Show the position on your own hand and name what matters.
items.twoStarDescription: Watch the other person try, and name one difference you can see.
items.threeStarDescription: Show the adjustment once, then let them decide whether it feels usable.

items.title: Teach a one-minute trick
items.description: Teach a trick that takes about a minute, and watch the learner do it.
items.oneStarDescription: Show the moves in order.
items.twoStarDescription: Watch them do it without taking the object back unless they ask.
items.threeStarDescription: Name one thing to change, or say it worked.

items.title: Teach one rule by moving a piece
items.description: Show this result: move one piece to show a single rule, then put it back.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: move one piece to show a single rule, then put it back.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: move one piece to show a single rule, then put it back.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: move one piece to show a single rule, then put it back.

items.title: Teach the end of the game first
items.description: Show this result: explain how the game ends before you explain a special piece.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so a watcher can see you start: explain how the game ends before you explain a special piece.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once, and leave it as it is: explain how the game ends before you explain a special piece.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you did not do, after this result: explain how the game ends before you explain a special piece.

items.title: Teach with the object in their hands
items.description: Teach one step while the object is in the learner's hands, not yours.
items.oneStarDescription: Give them the object before you explain.
items.twoStarDescription: Guide one step with words while they hold it.
items.threeStarDescription: Let them finish that step and say what you were about to grab.

items.title: Tell a beetle shape from a fly shape on a chart

items.oneStarDescription: Look and start this result: point to wing covers on the beetle picture and one pair of wings on the fly picture.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish the visible part: point to wing covers on the beetle picture and one pair of wings on the fly picture.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop before a guess. The result was: point to wing covers on the beetle picture and one pair of wings on the fly picture.

items.title: Tell a bulb from a seed
items.description: Point to a bulb and a seed and say one difference you can see.
items.oneStarDescription: Place one of each, or a photo of each.
items.twoStarDescription: Say a difference in size, layers, or shape.
items.threeStarDescription: Say which you would plant as which, from the label, or that the label is missing.

items.title: Tell a butterfly from a moth

items.twoStarDescription: Name the feature you used, such as the feelers or the wing rest.
items.threeStarDescription: Say what you could not see, and stop if the chart does not fit.

items.twoStarDescription: Say free column or flat against the wall.

items.title: Tell a cone from a needle bunch

items.twoStarDescription: Say cone or needles. A second person can see that this step happened: name it.
items.threeStarDescription: Find the other on the same tree or the ground beneath, or say it is not there.

items.title: Tell a group the time you will start

items.twoStarDescription: Make the change so someone else can check it: say the time and wait.
items.threeStarDescription: Leave the work so the next person can see what you did: say the time and wait.

items.title: Tell a guest what they may use
items.description: Tell a guest what they may use in the kitchen or the room, and what to leave.
items.oneStarDescription: Name the things they may use.
items.twoStarDescription: Name one thing you would like left alone.
items.threeStarDescription: Point to one thing they should not switch on, such as a hob, if it matters, without a repair lesson.

items.title: Tell a host you are leaving
items.description: Show this result: find the host, thank them, and leave.
items.oneStarDescription: Set up so you can do this: find the host, thank them, and leave.
items.twoStarDescription: Finish this once: find the host, thank them, and leave.
items.threeStarDescription: Stop and leave the result visible: find the host, thank them, and leave.

items.title: Tell a knit from a woven cloth
items.description: Tell a knit cloth from a woven cloth by the structure you can see or stretch.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to the loops or the crossed threads.
items.twoStarDescription: Stretch gently and say which one springs back more.
items.threeStarDescription: Name which is knit and which is woven, or say you are not sure.

items.title: Tell a knit stitch from a purl
items.description: On a knitted sample, point to a smooth stitch and a bumpy stitch.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to a V-shaped stitch.
items.twoStarDescription: Point to a bump on the other side or the same row.
items.threeStarDescription: Use a chart's words and say if the sample does not match.

items.oneStarDescription: Point to both thumbs. A second person can see that this step happened: find the thumbs.
items.twoStarDescription: Put them so the thumbs face each other when the palms are down.
items.threeStarDescription: Say which glove is the left.

items.title: Tell a mosaic from a fresco in a photo
items.description: Say whether a picture is made of pieces or painted onto a surface, using a photo or a work you can see.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to the surface. A second person can see that this step happened: look close.
items.twoStarDescription: Say mosaic or painted surface, and the clue.
items.threeStarDescription: If you cannot see the surface, say the photo is not enough.

items.title: Tell a needle leaf from a broad leaf

items.twoStarDescription: Sort at least four, and set aside one you will not force.

items.title: Tell a plucked note from a bowed one
items.description: Hear two string sounds and say which was plucked and which was bowed.
items.oneStarDescription: Listen to both before you answer.
items.twoStarDescription: Say which is plucked and which is bowed.
items.threeStarDescription: If one is unclear, say so.

items.title: Tell a portrait from a still life
items.description: Say whether a picture is mainly a person or mainly objects, and point to the clue.
items.oneStarDescription: Look at the picture. A second person can see that this step happened: look.
items.twoStarDescription: Say portrait or still life.
items.threeStarDescription: Point to the face or the objects that decided it.

items.title: Tell a preview from a review
items.description: Say whether a short text is selling a future showing or responding to a work the writer saw.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to a word that places the work in the future or in the past.
items.twoStarDescription: Point to one detail that could only come from seeing it, or write that there is none.
items.threeStarDescription: Label it preview or review, and write the clue you used.

items.title: Tell a QR code from a barcode
items.description: Point to a QR code and a barcode and say what each is for in one sentence.
items.oneStarDescription: Show one of each, or a photo of each.
items.twoStarDescription: Say the QR code can open a link and the barcode is a product number.
items.threeStarDescription: Say you are not checking whether the link is safe.

items.title: Tell a raw edge from a hemmed edge
items.description: Point to a raw edge and a hemmed edge on cloth you may handle.

items.twoStarDescription: Point to a folded finished edge.
items.threeStarDescription: Say which edge still needs a finish.

items.title: Tell a reed from an open mouthpiece
items.description: Point to a reed mouthpiece and a lip-blown open mouthpiece, or say you can see only one.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to a mouthpiece you may look at.
items.twoStarDescription: Say reed or open, from what you see.
items.threeStarDescription: Find the other, or write that you saw only one.

items.title: Tell a round arch from a pointed arch
items.description: Point to an arch and say whether the top is round or pointed.
items.oneStarDescription: Point to an arch from the street.
items.twoStarDescription: Say round or pointed. A second person can see that this step happened: name the top.
items.threeStarDescription: Find the other kind, or write that this street showed only one.

items.title: Tell a sewn binding from a glued one
items.description: Open a book and say whether you can see threads in the gutter or only glue.
items.oneStarDescription: Open the book at the middle.
items.twoStarDescription: Say whether you see stitches.
items.threeStarDescription: Say sewn, glued, or not sure.

items.title: Tell a short true story
items.description: Tell a true story with a start, a change, and an end a listener can retell.
items.oneStarDescription: Tell a true event that includes what changed from the beginning to the end.
items.twoStarDescription: Tell it again in fewer sentences and ask the listener what they still understood.
items.threeStarDescription: Say one true part you did not tell, and why you left it out.

items.title: Tell a simple leaf from a compound leaf
items.description: Say whether one leaf stalk holds one blade or several leaflets.
items.oneStarDescription: Follow one stalk back to the twig.
items.twoStarDescription: Say one blade or several leaflets.
items.threeStarDescription: Look for a bud at the base of the whole leaf, and say if you cannot see one.

items.title: Tell a slide brass from valves
items.description: From a photo or an instrument you may look at, say whether the brass instrument uses a slide or valves.

items.twoStarDescription: Say slide or valves. A second person can see that this step happened: name it.
items.threeStarDescription: Say you are not naming the piece of music.

items.title: Tell a still moment from motion blur

items.threeStarDescription: Say what looks as if it moved, without inventing a speed.

items.title: Tell a web from a nest
items.description: Point to a web and a nest, or say which one you cannot find.

items.threeStarDescription: Step back and say you will not touch it.

items.title: Tell damp ground from dry

items.twoStarDescription: Touch one spot or watch whether it wets a finger.
items.threeStarDescription: Say frost or dew, or that you are not sure.

items.twoStarDescription: Point to the longer side.
items.threeStarDescription: Turn a photo you may edit to the other orientation and say what got cut, or that nothing did.

items.title: Tell moss from lichen

items.oneStarDescription: Point to a green or gray patch on bark or stone.
items.twoStarDescription: Call it moss or lichen and name the clue, such as leaves or a crust.
items.threeStarDescription: Find the other, or write that this place showed only one.

items.oneStarDescription: For a non-hazardous device issue, record the symptom and check power, connections, settings and available error messages before changing anything.
items.twoStarDescription: Use a safe troubleshooting checklist to test at least two plausible causes, changing one variable at a time and recording the result.
